projectName: AI Todo App - Phase 1: Core App
description: Build a working todo list application with AI agent assistant, backed by Databricks Lakebase
objectives: Create functional todo CRUD operations via REST API
Implement React UI for task management
Connect backend to Databricks as primary database (Lakebase pattern)
Build basic LangGraph AI agent for natural language task creation
Validate Databricks as OLTP replacement (not just analytics)

userStories.title: Backend Configuration and Databricks Connection
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to set up the FastAPI backend with proper configuration management and establish a working connection to Databricks so that I can build on a solid foundation
acceptanceCriteria: FastAPI app initializes with proper project structure
Pydantic Settings loads environment variables from .env file
Databricks SQL Connector successfully connects to SQL Warehouse
Health check endpoint returns Databricks connection status
Error handling for missing credentials or connection failures
technicalNotes: Use pydantic-settings for config management
Databricks connector is synchronous - wrap in asyncio.to_thread() for FastAPI
Connection string format: server_hostname + http_path + access_token
Test with: SELECT 1 query to validate connection

userStories.title: Database Schema and Test Data Setup
userStories.description: As a developer, I need to create the necessary tables in Databricks and populate test data so that the API has data to work with
acceptanceCriteria: Tasks table exists in main.todo_app.tasks with correct schema
Users table exists in main.todo_app.users
At least one test user is created
Delta Lake ACID properties are enabled
Schema includes proper constraints (PK, NOT NULL, etc.)
SQL setup script is documented and repeatable
technicalNotes: Run SQL commands in Databricks SQL Editor
Use Delta Lake format (USING DELTA)
Enable Change Data Feed for future streaming (Phase 3)
Schema: task_id, user_id, title, description, status, priority, due_date, created_at, updated_at

userStories.title: Task CRUD API Endpoints
userStories.description: As a backend developer, I need REST API endpoints for creating, reading, updating, and deleting tasks so that the frontend can manage tasks
acceptanceCriteria: POST /tasks creates a new task and returns task object with generated ID
GET /tasks returns list of all tasks for a user
GET /tasks/{task_id} returns a single task by ID
PUT /tasks/{task_id} updates task fields and returns updated task
DELETE /tasks/{task_id} removes task and returns 204 No Content
All endpoints use Pydantic schemas for validation
Proper HTTP status codes (200, 201, 404, 422, 500)
Error responses include helpful error messages
technicalNotes: Use UUID for task_id generation
Validate user_id exists before creating task
Use Pydantic models in schemas.py as single source of truth
Wrap all DB operations in asyncio.to_thread()
Handle Databricks-specific errors (connection loss, query timeout)

userStories.title: Pydantic Schemas for Request/Response Validation
userStories.description: As a developer, I need well-defined Pydantic schemas to validate all API requests and responses so that data integrity is maintained
acceptanceCriteria: TaskCreate schema validates task creation requests
TaskUpdate schema validates partial updates (all fields optional except task_id)
TaskResponse schema formats task data for API responses
TaskStatus enum restricts values to: pending, in_progress, completed, cancelled
TaskPriority enum restricts values to: low, medium, high, urgent
Field validation includes length limits and format checks
Clear error messages on validation failures
technicalNotes: Use Field() with constraints (min_length, max_length, description)
Use Enum for categorical fields (status, priority)
due_date should be datetime | None
created_at and updated_at are auto-generated, not in Create schema

userStories.title: React Todo List UI
userStories.description: As a user, I need a clean web interface to view, create, update, and delete my tasks so that I can manage my todos visually
acceptanceCriteria: Task list displays all tasks with title, status, priority, due date
Add task form allows creating new tasks
Each task has edit and delete buttons
Task status can be toggled (pending ↔ completed)
Tasks are grouped by status (pending, completed)
UI updates immediately after API calls (optimistic updates)
Loading states shown during API calls
Error messages displayed on API failures
technicalNotes: Use React hooks (useState, useEffect) for state management
Use fetch or axios for API calls
Consider using React Hook Form for form validation
Style with Tailwind CSS or basic CSS
Component structure: App → TaskList → TaskItem, TaskForm

userStories.title: Basic AI Agent for Natural Language Task Creation
userStories.description: As a user, I want to create tasks using natural language (e.g., 'Remind me to buy milk tomorrow at 3pm') so that I don't have to fill out forms manually
acceptanceCriteria: POST /agent/chat endpoint accepts natural language input
Agent extracts task details: title, due_date from user message
Agent creates task via internal API call
Agent responds with confirmation message
Agent handles ambiguous input gracefully (asks clarifying questions)
Response is streamed back to client (Server-Sent Events or WebSocket)
Agent uses tool calling to invoke create_task function
technicalNotes: Use LangGraph for agent orchestration
Use OpenAI function calling (tools) for structured output
Model: gpt-4o-mini (cost-effective for simple tasks)
System prompt guides agent to extract task fields
Use response_format={'type': 'json_object'} for structured extraction
Wrap agent execution in asyncio to avoid blocking FastAPI

userStories.title: AI Agent Chat Interface in Frontend
userStories.description: As a user, I want a chat interface where I can talk to the AI agent to create tasks using natural language
acceptanceCriteria: Chat interface displays message history (user + agent)
User can type message and send to agent
Agent responses stream in real-time
Loading indicator while agent is thinking
Tasks created by agent appear in task list immediately
Chat interface is separate from task list (modal or sidebar)
technicalNotes: Use EventSource API for SSE streaming from backend
Or use WebSocket for bidirectional communication
Store chat history in local state (no backend persistence in Phase 1)
Component: AgentChat.jsx

userStories.title: API Testing and Validation
userStories.description: As a developer, I need automated tests for API endpoints to ensure reliability and catch regressions
acceptanceCriteria: Tests cover all CRUD endpoints (create, read, update, delete)
Tests verify Pydantic validation errors return 422 status
Tests verify 404 errors for non-existent tasks
Tests verify database writes succeed
Tests use pytest with pytest-asyncio
Tests can run against real Databricks (integration tests) or mocked DB (unit tests)
All tests pass before marking user story complete

Use httpx.AsyncClient for API testing
Consider using testcontainers or mocking DB for faster tests
Test file: tests/test_api.py

Environment variables are documented in .env.example
SQL setup script is documented with step-by-step instructions
API endpoints are documented (can use FastAPI auto-docs)
Common errors and troubleshooting tips are listed

Add backend/README.md if needed for detailed setup

functional: User can create, view, update, delete tasks via UI
AI agent successfully creates tasks from natural language in >80% of simple test cases
All API endpoints return correct status codes and data formats
technical: API response times < 500ms for CRUD operations
Agent response time < 3 seconds for simple task creation
Zero database connection errors during normal operation

Understand Databricks SQL Connector usage patterns
Understand OpenAI function calling for structured output

outOfScope: User authentication/authorization (hardcode test user for Phase 1)

technicalDecisions.decision: Use Databricks as primary database (Lakebase pattern)
technicalDecisions.rationale: Learn lakehouse as OLTP replacement. Eliminates ETL from app DB to warehouse. Unity Catalog provides governance.
OpenAI response_format guarantees valid JSON without wrapper text. Better for structured output.

technicalDecisions.decision: Use LangGraph instead of raw LangChain
technicalDecisions.rationale: LangGraph provides better state management and tool orchestration for multi-step agents. Easier to extend in later phases.
Databricks SQL Connector is synchronous. Wrapping in asyncio.to_thread() prevents blocking FastAPI event loop.

technicalDecisions.decision: Local development (no cloud deployment in Phase 1)
technicalDecisions.rationale: Focus on learning core concepts. Phase 6 will cover production deployment to Azure AKS.

risks.risk: Databricks SQL Warehouse auto-stops during development
risks.mitigation: Set auto-stop to 60+ minutes. Document how to restart warehouse.

risks.risk: OpenAI API rate limits or costs exceed budget
risks.mitigation: Use gpt-4o-mini (cheapest model). Set max_tokens=500 limit. Track usage daily.

risks.risk: Synchronous DB calls cause FastAPI performance issues
risks.mitigation: Always wrap DB calls in asyncio.to_thread(). Monitor response times. Consider connection pooling.

risks.risk: Agent fails to parse natural language correctly
risks.mitigation: Start with simple prompts. Add examples to system prompt. Phase 5 will add evaluation.
